items.summary: Introduction Real-time neural decoding is critical for precise neuromodulation, which is of increasing interest in the treatment of brain disorders. items.title: Technological neuropsychology: Assessing cognition in a digital world
items.summary: Clinical neuropsychology was forged in a pre-digital era, and many of its core instruments still bear that imprint. Patients are still commonly assessed with paper-and-pencil tests in quiet rooms, under conditions that only weakly approximate the technology-saturated environments in which cognition is now expressed. Over the past decade, the field has advanced substantially: tele-neuropsychology has broadened access, artificial intelligence has begun to support scoring and documentation, and calls to modernise neuropsychological assessment have intensified. items.summary: This article argues that the persistent burden of burnout reflects a fundamental conceptual problem—burnout continues to be framed primarily as an individual condition rather than as an occupational phenomenon shaped by interacting structural, organizational, and leadership conditions. Burnout has emerged as a major occupational health challenge. items.summary: Abstract EEG microstates are brief and discrete topographic patterns of electrical brain activity. Microstates last for 60–120 milliseconds, are thought to represent transient, quasi-stable neural networks, and traditionally four distinct classes (A-D) are distinguished. items.title: Glucocorticoid dynamics predict susceptibility and resilience to traumatic stress in male and female rats
items.summary: Introduction The mammalian stress response relies on tightly regulated HPA axis signaling, and disruptions in glucocorticoid feedback are implicated in stress-related disorders such as PTSD. Although many individuals experience trauma, only some develop pathology, suggesting that individual differences in glucocorticoid responsivity may help predict susceptibility or resilience. Here, we examined whether corticosterone (CORT) responses to a mild stressor predict behavioral outcomes following single-prolonged stress (SPS) in male and female rats. items.summary: Introduction Non-invasive imaging of brain function and energy supply is crucial for diagnosing and treating brain disorders. Conventional imaging struggles to capture altered relationships between energy supply and demand caused by brain diseases. items.title: Dissociable Intrinsic Connectivity Networks for Salience Processing and Executive Control
items.summary: Variations in neural circuitry, inherited or acquired, may underlie important individual differences in thought, feeling, and action patterns. Here, we used task-free connectivity analyses to isolate and characterize two distinct networks typically coactivated during functional MRI tasks. We identified a "salience network," anchored by dorsal anterior cingulate (dACC) and orbital frontoinsular cortices with robust connectivity to subcortical and limbic structures, and an "executive-control network" that links dorsolateral frontal and parietal neocortices. items.title: The Role of physical activity and exercise in college students' mental health
items.summary: The current review provides a comprehensive understanding of the links between physical activity and mental health outcomes. A total of 38 studies were included in this review. The PRISMA guideline was followed during the search and screening process. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Social Relationships and Mortality Risk: A Meta-analytic Review
items.summary: BACKGROUND: The quality and quantity of individuals' social relationships has been linked not only to mental health but also to both morbidity and mortality. OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk.
